tasks.instruction_text: Quick one on realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes: I want to mirror what I asked the assistant earlier — "I'm looking to buy a house in Staten Island, NY that has 4 or more bedrooms, a large lot, and access to top-rated schools. Can you help me find a listing that meets these criteria". The only piece that isn't on the visible filter row is 'Top-rated schools nearby', which is hidden behind the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in). Just turn that one on and apply it.

Looking at Staten Island homes on realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes — apply central A/C and master bedroom on first floor both. They live behind the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in); once you open it you'll see them as checkboxes. Don't forget to confirm.

Okay so, I've narrowed things down a bit but actually let me think... for the Staten Island homes search on realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes, I really want solar panels on. And honestly master bedroom on first floor is becoming a deal-breaker too — turn it on. Both toggles live under the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in) so you'll have to open that to find them; they're not in the visible filter dropdowns.

For my shortlist on realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes, narrow Staten Island homes down to ones that satisfy all three of: top-rated schools nearby, central A/C, and outside flood zone. Heads up — none of these are on the visible filter bar; you have to crack open the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in) and tick each one before hitting apply.
Quick read on realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes — out of the 20 Staten Island homes on the page, how many are listed under $659,000? Just the number is fine.

Hmm, on realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes, can you scan through the Staten Island homes listings and tell me — out of the ones flagged as 'Outside flood zone' on the listing cards, which is the CHEAPEST? Address + price. (That flag is normally something you'd toggle via the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in), but for now I just want you to eyeball the cards.)

On realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes, which is more common across the Staten Island homes: listings tagged 'Large lot (0.25+ acres)' or 'Finished basement'? Give me both counts so I can decide which feature to filter on. (Both attributes are normally hidden under the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in), so you'd toggle them there — but right now I just want a head-count from the card flags.)

Hop into realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes, pop open the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in), and tick 'Renovated kitchen' — that toggle is NOT on the main filter row, it's hidden inside. After you apply it, tell me which of the matching Staten Island homes is the cheapest (address + price).

On realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes for Staten Island homes: open the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in) and flip on BOTH renovated kitchen AND outside flood zone. Neither shows up in the standard dropdowns; they're only inside that hidden panel. After both are applied, tell me how many listings match in total.

I might be overthinking this but on realtor.com Staten Island NY 4-bedroom homes, this is a longer one. Inside the vertical red 'MORE FILTERS' tab pinned to the right edge of the page (it slides a hidden side panel in) (the hidden filter panel — NOT the main bar), flip on renovated kitchen, central A/C, and 2-car garage. All of those are hidden in there. Once they're all applied, look at what's left and tell me the address + sqft of the single LARGEST homes still showing.
